preamble: In Central and Eastern Scandinavian dialects a rhotic followed by [s] fuses with it into a single retroflex fricative [ʂ]. The tongue tip, already curled back for the apical [r], carries that retraction onto the following sibilant, and the rhotic itself disappears.

examples.note: Swedish 'rapids'. Not found in Southern Swedish and other dialects with a uvular r.

sources: Riad, T. (2014). The Phonology of Swedish. Oxford University Press.
Kristoffersen, G. (2000). The Phonology of Norwegian. Oxford University Press.
Ladefoged, P., & Maddieson, I. (1996). The Sounds of the World's Languages.
